subject.title: Discord account-to-agent routing falls back to default agent instead of matching by account name

question: Should unmatched Discord accountIds implicitly route to a configured same-named agent, or should explicit bindings remain the only supported account-to-agent routing contract?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible, but fallback semantics affect security boundaries, provider/model selection, session state, and existing multi-account upgrade behavior.

options.title: Approve Guarded Fallback
options.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with diagnostics, docs, regression tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Keep Explicit Bindings Only
options.body: Leave runtime routing unchanged and add docs, doctor, or status warnings for Discord accounts that look intended to bind to same-named agents.

options.title: Use Existing PR As Source Material
options.body: Treat the existing unmerged PR as a sketch, but require conflict repair, guard checks, diagnostics, and real Discord proof before adoption.

recommendation.title: Approve Guarded Fallback
recommendation.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with diagnostics, docs, regression tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is the original multi-agent routing and provider surface introduction.
